newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil hitches ride on crude, French strike.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil hitches ride on crude, French strike.

text.p: Crude's strength and concerns over the continued strike at Elf's three refineries in France helped knock fuel oil prices higher.
Support was also derived from talk of strong Romanian demand and two tenders in the Mediterranean to be awarded tomorrow or later this week.

High sulphur cracked barges hiked up $4 a tonne to $126 fob ARA supported by improved bunker demand. Levels eased off during the course of the day to $123-124 Cargoes were pegged stronger up to $124 a tonne cif NWE, but little activity was seen.

Traders said there were moves to cover any potential shorts that may be caused by the labour dispute at Elf's refineriers. Dealers were already saying that some of Elf's expected cargoes may be delayed or lost altogether.
Low sulphur cargoes also moved higher with a December paper deal done at $135 fob. "The whole complex is stronger, so there's no reason why low sulphur shouldn't go up as well," said one trader.
Strong natural gas prices in the U.S. should help to keep American low sulphur at home, giving support to the European market.
